thread:
sasha: Heads-up — canary for release/weights-roll-2026 is showing a spike in decode failures and malformed tokens on redwood-v3-small.canary. Error rate ~3.4% on /v1/generate. Noticed outputs with repeated � or broken subwords.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-0427-1 · Severity: P2 · Pager paged to @mike
mike: seeing it, joining. Any immediate customer impact? :eyes:
sasha: visibility shows a single large customer making lots of calls, but we've got a few internal tests failing too. Looks like tokenizer offset/special-token mapping is off compared to prod weights.
elaine: I can pull the artifact diffs. My hunch: the vocab.json used in the canary build wasn't the expected one — maybe an aliasing issue during artifact promotion.
jordan: @elaine which bundle id did the CI promote? I thought we pinned vocab -> hash: v3-20260427-abc123 but artifact tag for weights is v3-20260427-abc123 as well. Could be a packaging bug.
elaine: pulling now. Running quick check:

```
# local quick check
python tools/tokenizer_check.py --vocab /artifacts/vocab.json --sample "Hello, world!"
```

elaine: result: token ids mismatch with baseline. Baseline vocab hash: a1f3... ; canary vocab hash: b9c7... — not the same.
mike: can we flip traffic? What are options? rollback? kill flag? ops-bot can flip canary off?
ops-bot: ACTION: flipping feature flag rollout/canary-weight-2026 -> OFF (requested by @mike)
ops-bot: feature flag flipped successfully. Routing policy updated to route 100% to redwood-v3-small.stable
sasha: routing moved. Metrics dropping back to baseline for 5xx, but I still see tokenization anomalies in some cached KV entries from canary nodes.
elaine: on that — canary nodes that served the bad vocab will have cached KV states tied to that tokenizer. We need to evict KV on canary nodes and recycle them to be safe.
jordan: start a controlled recycle and eviction job. Label it "canary-evict-20260427" and run with concurrency 10% to avoid churn.
mike: @jordan please coordinate. @cust-success can you check if that big customer saw garbled outputs? We should proactively reach out.
cust-success: I've opened a support ticket and pinged the customer. They confirmed a handful of malformed responses and logged user complaints. They're asking if data was exposed — reassure: no, this is encoding mismatch only.
elaine: plan:
1) Evict KV and recycle canary nodes (low concurrency) — running now.
2) Re-push correct vocab artifact and re-deploy canary after verification.
3) Rollback weights if any further corruption seen.

I'll also add a checksum gate on promotion.
sasha: logs from canary recycle job:

```
2026-04-27T15:15:22Z evict/kv: node canary-12 evicted 1243 entries
2026-04-27T15:16:01Z recycle: draining canary-12 -> restart ok
```

mike: good. What's ETA to repro and verify corrected vocab? elaine?
elaine: pulling verified vocab from staging and running tokenization diff now. Should have green in ~8m.
jordan: hold public rollback for now since flag flip routed traffic back. We'll only roll weights if anomalies persist after KV eviction and vocab repair.
elaine: token diffs done: green. Pushing new artifact tag v3-20260427-expectedvocab -> promoting to canary but will keep traffic 0% initially and run the sampler.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: promoted artifact v3-20260427-expectedvocab to canary (traffic 0%)
elaine: running smoke with 1000 synthetic requests:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v3-small.canary","prompt":"test"}' | jq .
```

elaine: smoke looks clean, no malformed tokens in sample.
sasha: we should re-run customer repro on staging and offer a clean endpoint for them to validate.
cust-success: customer accepted a test endpoint and confirmed fixes. They appreciated the quick action.
mike: marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep monitoring for 60m then close. Follow-ups: add promotion checksum gate, eviction runbook, and add alert for tokenizer-hash-drift.
jordan: opening follow-up ticket: PROD-OPS-2026-209 "artifact-promotion checksum validation + release gating" assigned to eng-release.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-0427-1 mitigated · status: monitoring · assigned: @mike
sasha: thanks team. Postmortem please with timeline + root cause (artifact alias bug) and action items.
mike: agreed. I'll own the postmortem. Closing status in 1hr if stable. :white_check_mark:
